answers.label: B
answers.working:
The cockroach (an arthropod) has an **open circulatory system**: blood (haemolymph) is pumped into open spaces called sinuses and bathes the organs directly. Its excretory organs are **Malpighian tubules**, which remove nitrogenous wastes from the haemolymph.

The earthworm (an annelid) has a **closed circulatory system**: blood always stays inside vessels. Its excretory organs are **nephridia**.

So the two groups are open circulation, Malpighian tubules, cockroach (1, 4, 6) and closed circulation, earthworm, nephridia (2, 3, 5). So the answer is option (B).

answers.label: A
answers.value: Plant A turns redder than Plant B.
answers.working:
Water rises up the xylem mainly because of the **transpiration pull**: as water evaporates from the leaves, the column of water in the xylem is pulled upward, and the dissolved dye travels with it.

Transpiration is fast in dry air, because the difference in water vapour between the leaf and the air is large. In high humidity this difference is small, so transpiration (and hence the pull) is slow.

Plant A, in dry conditions, therefore draws up more dyed water and its tissues turn red faster and more strongly than those of Plant B. So the answer is option (A).

answers.working:
Once the medium-seeded plants are gone, the only food left is large seeds. Within the finch population, birds whose beaks happen to be a little larger can crack large seeds better, so they survive and leave more offspring.

Over generations this **directional selection** shifts the average beak size of the population towards larger beaks (this is what was actually seen in Darwin's finches after droughts). Smaller beaks would be selected against, and the population need not die out because some variation in beak size already exists. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: D
answers.working:
A population limited by food and housing follows **logistic growth**:

\(\dfrac{dN}{dt} = rN\left(\dfrac{K-N}{K}\right)\)

Here \(N = 100\), the intrinsic rate \(r = 0.1\) per year and the carrying capacity \(K = 200\).

\(\dfrac{dN}{dt} = 0.1 \times 100 \times \dfrac{200-100}{200} = 10 \times 0.5 = 5\) per year.

Without the limit (exponential growth) it would be \(rN = 10\) per year, but only half the carrying capacity is still free, so the growth is halved. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: A
answers.value: The inner and outer membranes have identical sets of enzymes.
answers.working:
The two mitochondrial membranes are very different. The **outer membrane** is smooth and freely permeable, while the **inner membrane** carries the enzymes of the electron transport chain and ATP synthase, which the outer membrane does not have. So the statement that both membranes have identical enzymes is wrong.

The other statements are true: the matrix contains a single circular DNA molecule and 70S ribosomes, and the inner membrane folds inward to form cristae, which increase its surface area. So the answer is option (A).

answers.label: B
answers.value: Cells in this stage are metabolically active but not dividing.
answers.working:
Cells that leave the cell cycle after the G1 phase enter an inactive stage called the **quiescent stage (G0)**. Such cells remain **metabolically active** (they carry out their normal functions) but no longer proliferate, unless they are called upon to do so. Many nerve cells and heart muscle cells stay in G0.

They are not dying, they are not highly proliferative, and they are not metabolically inactive. So the answer is option (B).

answers.label: D
answers.value: Administering anti-Rh antibodies to a Rh -ve mother after her first Rh +ve child birth.
answers.working:
**Erythroblastosis foetalis** arises when an Rh negative mother carries an Rh positive foetus. During the first delivery some foetal blood enters the mother's blood, and she starts making anti-Rh antibodies. In a later Rh positive pregnancy these antibodies cross the placenta and destroy the foetus's red blood cells.

It is prevented by giving the **Rh negative mother anti-Rh antibodies immediately after the delivery of her first Rh positive child**. These antibodies remove the foetal Rh antigens before her own immune system can make antibodies against them.

An Rh positive woman is never at risk, and giving the antibodies before the first pregnancy does not cover the moment of exposure, which is the delivery. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: C
answers.working:
In the electron transport chain, electrons from NADH and \(\mathrm{FADH_2}\) pass through complexes I to IV, with cytochrome c carrying them between complexes III and IV. At the end, cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV) hands the electrons to **oxygen**, which combines with protons to form water.

Oxygen is the **terminal (final) electron acceptor**. FAD and \(\mathrm{NAD^+}\) are electron carriers at the start, and cytochrome c is an intermediate carrier. So the answer is option (C).

answers.label: D
answers.working:
Lymphocytes are made and mature in the **primary lymphoid organs**: the bone marrow and the **thymus**. Immature T lymphocytes move from the bone marrow to the thymus, where they mature into antigen-sensitive T cells.

The spleen and Peyer's patches are **secondary lymphoid organs**, where already mature lymphocytes meet antigens. The liver is not a lymphoid organ in adults. Of the options given, only the thymus is a primary lymphoid organ holding immature lymphocytes. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: C
answers.value: \(K_M\) is the concentration of substrate when the velocity of the reaction is half that of the maximal velocity.
answers.working:
Put \(V_0 = \dfrac{V_{max}}{2}\) into the equation:

\(\dfrac{V_{max}}{2} = V_{max} \cdot \dfrac{[S]}{K_M + [S]}\)

So \(K_M + [S] = 2[S]\), which gives \([S] = K_M\).

Thus \(K_M\) is the **substrate concentration at which the reaction velocity is half the maximal velocity**. It has the units of concentration of substrate, not of enzyme and not of velocity, so the other options are wrong. So the answer is option (C).

answers.value: Adequate rest and a balanced diet for at least three days.
answers.working:
Rhinoviruses are **viruses**. Antibiotics such as streptomycin and amoxycillin act on bacteria (their cell wall, ribosomes and so on) and have no effect on a virus, so options (A), (B) and (C) do not treat the cause. Using antibiotics against a viral cold only encourages antibiotic resistance.

The common cold is self-limiting: the body's own immune system clears it in a few days. Rest and a balanced diet support that immune response. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: B
answers.working:
**Oogenesis** begins during the embryonic (foetal) development of the female. Within the developing ovary, oogonia (egg mother cells) form and divide, then enter meiosis I and stop at prophase I as **primary oocytes**. No more oogonia are formed or added after birth.

At puberty the primary oocytes resume development a few at a time, and meiosis I is completed only just before ovulation. So puberty and ovulation are later stages, not the start. So the answer is option (B).

answers.label: A
answers.value: It is multilayered and mainly protects from chemical and mechanical stresses.
answers.working:
A **compound epithelium** is made of more than one layer of cells. Because of this it has little role in secretion and absorption; its main function is to **protect against chemical and mechanical stresses**. It covers the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the buccal cavity and pharynx, the inner lining of the ducts of salivary glands and of pancreatic ducts.

Secretion and absorption are jobs of simple epithelia, and binding tissues together is the job of connective tissue. So the answer is option (A).

answers.working:
Cross red (RR) with white (rr): the F1 is all Rr, which is **pink** because neither allele is fully dominant (**incomplete dominance**).

Selfing the F1 (Rr x Rr) gives the genotypes RR : Rr : rr in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1.

Since each genotype has its own colour (RR red, Rr pink, rr white), the phenotype ratio is also red : pink : white = 1 : 2 : 1. The 3 : 1 phenotype ratio appears only with complete dominance. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: A
answers.value: All three RE1, RE2 and RE3 digested DNA.
answers.working:
Two DNA ends can be joined by DNA ligase if their single-stranded **sticky ends** are complementary. So find the overhang each enzyme leaves.

In every case the top strand is cut after the 1st base and the bottom strand after its 5th base (that is, just before the 1st base of the top strand read from the other side). This leaves a 4-base 5' overhang made of the middle four bases:

| Enzyme | Site | Overhang |
|---|---|---|
| RE1 | A^AGCTT | AGCT |
| RE2 | C^AGCTG | AGCT |
| RE3 | G^AGCTC | AGCT |

All three enzymes leave the same overhang 5'-AGCT-3', and AGCT is its own complement (palindromic). So an RE1 end pairs with an RE1, RE2 or RE3 end equally well and can be ligated to any of them. The outer bases differ, but they are already double stranded and do not affect pairing of the sticky ends. So the answer is option (A).
